native_result.query: What kind of demographic disparities exist in median wealth in 1985 among individuals who were ever incarcerated?
native_result.HypoA: Gender disparities exist in median wealth in 1985 among individuals who were ever incarcerated, with males having higher median wealth than females.
native_result.HypoB: Among NLSY79 respondents who were ever incarcerated between 1985 and 1994 (N=289), median wealth in 1985 was strongly stratified by race — White respondents had the highest median ($2,200; n=69), Black respondents roughly one-seventh as much ($320; n=159), and Hispanic respondents effectively zero ($0; n=61) — and within this same ever-incarcerated subgroup men had a substantially higher median wealth ($1,000; n=252) than women ($0; n=37).
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded data/nls_incarceration_processed.csv (12,013 rows, no nulls). Filtered to ever_jailed==1 (N=289). Sorted by median to determine the direction of disparity. Computed the within-race ever_jailed-vs-never_jailed median comparison as contextual evidence (not the headline). Computed race x sex cell sizes within ever_jailed==1 and disclosed small-cell (<=20) groups as limitations. Reported groups use 'hispanic' (matches dataset description); raw column encodes 'hipanic' (disclosed). No inflation adjustment and no survey weights applied.
